We look for mission-driven candidates who have a desire to advance the fight against cancer and make a difference in the lives of patients diagnosed with cancer every day.

Our Mission

People who live with cancer – those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it – are at the heart of every decision we make. Bringing the most innovative medical minds together with the most passionate caregivers in their communities, we are transforming care and personalizing treatment. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world.

Our Accounts Receivable Analyst is responsible for the collection of client receivables in accordance with contractual agreements. This includes review, maintenance and resolution of disputes, review of Clinical Trial revenue and expenses, review of study accounts receivable aging, patient accounts and pass through invoices, study finance trackers, patient trackers and contracts, as well as interaction with various departments in order to determine the validity of charges as well as the collection of those charges from sponsors.

Additionally, this position provides assistance to the Finance and Budget & Contracts departments on specifically identified projects and tasks listed below. This often involves analyzing multiple documents and often complex data to determine collectability of receivables.

This is a fully remote position based in the US; relocation assistance and visa sponsorship are not available.

Duties include but are not limited to:

  • Monitor assigned accounts: review aging, look for irregularities, non-payments, and delayed payments in customer accounts

  • Contact Sponsors/CROs via phone to follow on unpaid/open invoices and ensure timely payments are received

  • Investigate and resolve sponsor, patient and customer disputes

  • ​Maintaining a strong business relationship with the Sponsors/CROs as the primary contact and voice for Sarah Cannon Research Institute in regards to payment of receivables

  • Reconcile financial study data with data provided by Sponsors/CROs as needed.

  • Review, interpret and discuss contracts internally and with clients to assist with resolving payment or dispute issues

  • Review medical procedure invoices in relation to the contracts to determine eligibility for reimbursement of costs

  • Identify, report on and work with supervisor to resolve trends that negatively impact payment or workflows

  • Work with other departments (i.e. Accounting, Treasury, Contracting) to resolve billing questions as needed.

  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications for success include:

Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) is one of the world’s leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials. Join Our Team as Associate Editor at Canada’s National Observer

Reports to: Jimmy Thomson, Editor-in-Chief

Compensation range: $80,000 - $90,000 annually depending on experience

Location: Remote

Term: Full-time, permanent

Hours: Mon - Fri, 12 - 8pm Eastern Time / 9am-5pm Pacific Time

Status: Management role in a unionized workplace (this position is non-union)

About CNO

Whatbegan at a dining room tablein Vancouver in 2008 is now one of Canada's most decorated independent newsrooms.

Observer Media Group launched Vancouver Observer first, then Canada's National Observer in 2015, betting that excellent reporting and accountability journalism could thrive outside legacy media. In 2017, CNO became the first digital-only publication in Canadian history to win a National Newspaper Award and receive a Michener citation for public service journalism. "The little engine that could," then-Governor General David Johnston called it.

As we've grown, the awards have kept coming, and so has the impact. CNO investigations have forced government resignations, exposed dysfunction in the regulatory system overseeing a $15-billion pipeline, and revealed disinformation campaigns targeting local democracies. We have also shone a light on the best of Canadian innovation and solutions. In an era of climate crisis and coordinated disinformation, excellent accountability journalism has never mattered more.

Today, CNO covers Canada's changing climate from newsrooms in Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Montreal, and Ottawa, with more than 35,000 articles published. Last year we launched Civic Searchlight — our popular "superpower for democracy" — and earned ten new journalism award nominations this spring alone, including the inaugural Hinton Award for AI Safety Reporting from the Canadian Journalism Foundation.

The role

Canada’s National Observer seeks a talented editor with journalism and management experience to support the next phase of our award-winning journalism. You’re the right person for the job if you are keen to find new ways to shape important stories about the environment, climate, energy and politics. We seek a strong writer, editor and headline writer who can package our stories for maximum appeal and impact.

This is a leadership role with management and oversight responsibilities within a unionized workplace. This position is excluded from the bargaining unit.

The successful applicant will manage staff Monday through Friday between 12pm and 8pm Eastern Time / 9am and 5pm Pacific Time. The working hours are non-negotiable.

Daily responsibilities

  • Manage reporters in the afternoons
  • Supervise evening copy/newsletters
  • Focus on writing compelling headlines
  • Manage project budgets
  • Negotiate freelance contractor agreements
  • Manage editorial calendar, ensuring deadlines are met and quality is maintained
  • Help design and implement CNO’s project work
  • Fill in for EIC as required during vacations and sick days
  • Find compelling visuals, improve photography photo editing tools
  • Package stories for social media
  • Provide vacation relief for editors and newsletter editor
  • Recruit, hire and manage journalists and editors

Basic requirements

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in journalism
  • Strong understanding of politics, climate change and disinformation
  • Excellent editorial skills with a track record of impactful storytelling
  • Experience in a leadership or management role
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively and manage deadlines
  • Ace headline, story packaging and copy editing skills
  • Able to navigate a fast-paced work environment with flexibility, professionalism, and kindness

What we offer

  • Sun Life extended health package
  • Employer matching RSP
  • Benefits including one month of vacation, personal and sick days and equipment budget
  • Career development, mentorship and opportunity over time to take on a larger leadership role in the organization
  • Conference and training support
  • Subscriptions to other news sources and industry magazines

How to apply — Please read carefully

Upload your resume, a cover letter and three writing samples to the Bamboo Portal link

Requirements before applying: read Canada's National Observer and explore the site. Sign up for our newsletters. It costs $1 to subscribe for a month — subscribe and see how things work. Your cover letter should demonstrate your research abilities, your writing voice, and your understanding of the company. Sign up for Civic Searchlight and use it so you understand this as well. If you haven’t done a serious deep dive into what we do, and how we do it, you aren’t ready to apply.

A note on AI: Do not send us an AI-generated CV and cover letter. We want to hear your voice and see your work experience laid out clearly. In your cover letter, make it clear why you'd want to work for Canada's National Observer.

This post will remain open until we find the right candidate, but we hope to have someone in place by October.

Canada's National Observer is committed to building a team that reflects the country we cover. We actively welcome applications from Indigenous, Black, and racialized candidates, women, 2SLGBTQ+ people, and people with disabilities. Our Vancouver newsroom is located on the unceded traditional territories of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam), Sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Squamish), and səlilwətaɬ (Tsleil-Waututh) Nations and the land we live on inspires the work we do.

Salary: $80,000 - $90,0000 annually

raw.excerpt: About UsAbacus Insights is transforming how data works for health plans.
raw.description:
About Us

Abacus Insights is transforming how data works for health plans. Our mission is simple: make healthcare data usable, so the people responsible for care and cost decisions can act faster, with confidence.

We help health plans break down data silos to create a single, trusted data foundation. That foundation powers better decisions—so plans can improve outcomes, reduce waste, and deliver better experiences for members and providers alike. Backed by $100M from top investors, we’re tackling big challenges in an industry that’s ready for change. Our platform enables GenAI use cases by delivering clean, connected, and reliable healthcare data to support automation, prioritization, and decision workflows—and it’s why we are leading the way.

Our innovation begins with people. We are bold, curious, and collaborative—because the best ideas come from working together. We embrace the thoughtful use of AI and automation to drive innovation and efficiency, and we look for individuals who are curious and adaptable—those excited to leverage emerging technologies to enhance how we work—while keeping human insight, connection, and our clients at the center of every decision.

Ready to make an impact? Join us and let’s build the future together.

About the Role

Abacus Insights is at the forefront of transforming how health plans harness their data, and we are looking for a driven project leader to join our Implementation Program Management Office and help us deliver on that mission. You will lead complex, high-visibility IT projects across the US healthcare payer space, working at the intersection of cutting-edge cloud technology and one of the most consequential industries in the country.

You will own end-to-end delivery across a portfolio of client implementations, partnering with technical, clinical, and client-facing teams to solve hard problems and move fast without sacrificing quality. The work is real, the stakes are high, and the impact is visible.

For the right person, this role is also a launching pad — offering a clear path into senior PMO leadership, deep exposure to modern cloud-based data infrastructure, and a front-row seat to the future of healthcare technology at a company that is growing quickly and building something that lasts.

Your day to day

  • Manage end-to-end delivery of multiple large-scale projects or multiple smaller projects, ensuring timelines, scope, and quality are consistently achieved
  • Coordinate closely with Client Delivery Managers to understand client requirements and translate them into delivery objectives, milestones, dependencies, and sequencing that support an accurate and effective project schedule.
  • Apply industry standard project management practices across Schedule Management, Risk Management, Communications Management, and Stakeholder Engagement to improve delivery predictability, transparency, and cross-functional accountability.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional technical teams and client teams to understand delivery needs, constraints, and dependencies, then translate those inputs into clear business-facing decisions, status updates, mitigation plans, and executive-level project health reporting.
  • Own integrated project schedule management, including work plan development, milestone tracking, dependency management, critical path visibility, variance reporting, and alignment to client requirements.
  • Maintain disciplined risk and issue management practices, including RAID log ownership, proactive risk identification, mitigation planning, escalation path management, and follow-through on issue resolution.
  • Conduct detailed resource planning and capacity management to support realistic delivery commitments and schedule execution.
  • Facilitate regular status meetings to maintain project health visibility, confirm decisions and next steps, and ensure timely escalation of risks, issues, and dependencies.

What you bring to the team

  • Delivery Leadership: 10+ years leading technically complex IT projects and programs, with 8+ years in a dedicated Project Manager role and a consistent track record of on-time, high-quality delivery.
  • End-to-End Project Governance: Proven ability to drive projects through the full lifecycle — initiation through handover — using standard PMO artifacts including Project Charter, RAID, RACI, schedules, and status reporting.
  • Healthcare & Client Delivery: Demonstrated experience delivering healthcare IT implementations, with payer-side experience strongly preferred. Able to set and hold clear client expectations around scope, timelines, dependencies, and outcomes.
  • Agile & Hybrid Delivery: Comfortable managing in hybrid environments that combine Agile team execution with milestone-based planning, schedule governance, and structured stakeholder reporting.
  • Technical Acumen: Experience coordinating across software development, data engineering, system integration, QA, and architecture functions — with enough technical fluency to make informed calls on risks and trade-offs.
  • Risk & Dependency Management: Strong instincts for proactively identifying, tracking, and escalating risks, issues, and cross-functional dependencies. No surprises to stakeholders.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills across client, leadership, and cross-functional audiences. Comfortable defending a position, driving decisions, and holding team members accountable.
  • Tools & AI Enablement: Hands-on experience with Smartsheet, Jira, and AI agentic tools to support schedule management, backlog coordination, RAID tracking, and stakeholder reporting.

What we would like to see, but not required

  • US Healthcare implementation experience, with direct exposure to healthcare payer environments, enabling faster onboarding and effective client engagement within Abacus’ payer‑focused delivery model
  • Experience working for or with a US Medicaid payer.
  • Formal project management certification such as PMP® or PRINCE2®, demonstrating strong grounding in structured delivery governance, planning, and control
  • Certified Scrum Master (CSM) or equivalent Agile certification, supporting effective collaboration with Product, Engineering, and QA teams in Agile or hybrid delivery models

Compensation: Compensation for this role is based on experience, skills, and location, and includes base salary plus eligibility for performance bonuses and equity grants.

What you’ll get in return

  • Unlimited paid time off – recharge when you need it
  • Work from anywhere – flexibility to fit your life
  • Comprehensive health coverage – multiple plan options to choose from
  • Equity for every employee – share in our success
  • Growth-focused environment – your development matters here
  • Home office setup allowance – one-time support to get you started
  • Monthly cell phone allowance – stay connected with ease

Our Commitment as an Equal Opportunity Employer

As a mission-led technology company helping to drive better healthcare outcomes, Abacus Insights believes that the best innovation and value we can bring to our customers comes from diverse ideas, thoughts, experiences, and perspectives. Therefore, we dedicate resources to building diverse teams and providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants. Abacus prohibits discrimination and harassment regarding race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

At the heart of who we are is a commitment to continuously and intentionally building an inclusive culture—one that empowers every team member across the globe to do their best work and bring their authentic selves. We carry that same commitment into our hiring process, aiming to create an interview experience where you feel comfortable and confident showcasing your strengths. If there’s anything we can do to support that—big or small—please let us know.

Overview

Otter Products is currently recruiting for a Sr. National Account Manager to join our Sales team! This individual will manage sales activity for a key account for OtterBox. In this role, you will be a member of an incredibly talented Sales team. You can be based in Fort Collins, CO or remotely in the US.

As a Sr. National Account Manager you will be responsible for the strategic direction and management of assigned account(s) and will be accountable to deliver revenue and/or profitability targets. The ability to develop and grow strong relationships with key accounts and other stakeholders is critical. In addition to selling, this role will be responsible for activities such as forecasting and budget management. This role will require cross-functional collaboration and leadership.

The ideal candidate will possess strong decision making abilities, business acumen, and analytical skills. Experience working with major accounts in a sales capacity is highly preferred. Does this sounds like you? If so, keep reading!

About Otter Products

At Otter Products, we protect what’s important. From our founder’s garage in 1998 to the global technology leader we are today, Otter Products continues to drive growth through innovation and sense of purpose. Through our industry-leading brands – OtterBox and OtterCares – we provide our partners and customers the number one selling and most trusted products in our categories. Our founder’s core values are still at the heart of everything we do. We measure our success not just by business results, but by our ability to give back to our communities and strengthen opportunities for all. To learn more, visit www.otterbox.com/en-us/careers.html

    • Oversee account, channel or vertical specific training
  • C-Level Engagement
    • Attend meetings, check-ins and provide updates as required
    • Partner with the leadership team to drive strategic initiatives

  • Support and maintain a positive safety culture by following all safety policies and procedures and actively contributing to a safe working environment.

Qualifications

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic or status protected by law. Additionally, for eligible employees, we offer accrued paid time off based on seniority, volunteer time off, parental leave, bereavement leave, company holidays, and years of service awards. raw.title: Staff Software Engineer

raw.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Recovering entrepreneur? Frustrated with bureaucracy? Want to write the roadmap, not inherit one?

We're hiring across multiple levels and verticals. The nice thing about growing 30%+ at ~$2B ARR is that we need great engineers everywhere, and we have the room to shape the role around the right person. You build like a founder. We give you the platform to do it at scale.

About the role:

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) sits at the center of hardware, software, AI, and the physical world. The platform processes 25+ trillion data points annually from IoT sensors, cameras, and connected devices across thousands of organizations, and that dataset is compounding: it grew from 4 trillion to 25+ trillion in four years. We're still early in turning that data into the products that will define how physical operations run, and we're hiring the engineers who will build what comes next.

We're approaching ~$2B ARR growing 30%+ year over year, with 96% of our largest customers on two or more products. The fastest-growing divisions at Samsara are tackling the hardest, most ambiguous problems at the company: building new products from scratch, applying AI and ML to massive real-world datasets, and shipping capabilities that change how organizations maintain equipment, manage fleets, and run day-to-day operations. Most of this work is zero-to-one, at billion-dollar scale.

We're looking for software engineers who want to define what ships next. Leveling is broad and flexible: we're hiring from Senior through Principal, across platform and product, and we're open to shaping scope around the right person's strengths and interests. That window won't stay open long.

This role is remote and open to candidates residing in the US. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world. The software you build will have real-world stakes: helping keep the lights on, getting food into grocery stores, keeping workers safe. What ships here isn't metrics on a dashboard. It shows up on the loading dock, the job site, and the dispatch floor.
  • You want to build, not maintain. Samsara is in full growth mode. We're building new systems from scratch, not babysitting old ones. You'd own entire problem spaces end to end, with the autonomy to set direction from day one.
  • You want to work where AI meets the physical world. Samsara has spent a decade building the largest proprietary dataset for physical operations. More connected assets generate more data, more data trains better models, better models drive more value, and more value wins more assets. The market and the opportunity here are what set us apart, not just the models.
  • You believe customers are more than a number. Samsara engineers have a rare closeness to end users. You'll participate in customer interviews, collaborate with product managers and customer success, and use that context to build products that solve real problems operators face every day.
  • You have the curiosity and drive to figure it out. We're looking for people who take pride in their work and get things done at all costs. The engineers who thrive here don't wait to be told what to build. They define it, ship it, and own the outcome. The rate-limiting step on our teams isn't tooling or process. It's ambition.

In this role, you will:

  • Take ownership of technically complex, mission-critical areas and run with them. We want to point you in a direction and show up to the demo meeting impressed, not spend our weeks managing the details.
  • Define and drive technical strategy for new products and platform capabilities, from backend services and APIs to the customer-facing UI.
  • Design and ship full-stack features end to end. You'll work across backend, frontend, and potentially mobile to deliver AI-powered products that solve real operational problems.
  • Partner with product, design, and customer-facing teams to translate ambiguous, real-world problems into clear technical plans and measurable outcomes.
  • Build and scale the systems behind AI-driven products, including data ingestion, APIs, and the workflows that put intelligence into the hands of operators.
  • Raise the bar for the engineers around you through code reviews, design reviews, technical mentorship, and by setting a standard for quality, velocity, and craft.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8+ years of experience in software design and development, including building and operating production systems at scale.
  • Strong full-stack fundamentals. You're comfortable working across backend services, APIs, and frontend (web or mobile) to ship complete products.
  • Proficiency in modern languages and frameworks (Go, Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, React, or similar).
  • Demonstrated experience leading cross-team or cross-org projects from inception through rollout, including managing ambiguity, driving alignment, and delivering measurable impact.
  • Experience building AI-powered or data-driven products. You don't need to train models, but you know how to take AI capabilities and turn them into products customers love.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • A track record of building: zero-to-one products, systems you left in a meaningfully better place, or hard problems you refused to let stay unsolved.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience shipping AI-powered features in production, whether that's LLM-based products, agentic workflows, recommendation systems, or other customer-facing AI.
  • Comfort with modern AI-augmented development workflows (Cursor, LLMs, etc.) to multiply your output and accelerate delivery.
  • Background working with real-world operational data (telematics, sensor data, work orders, inspections) or a strong interest in learning the domain.
  • A proven track record of mentoring senior engineers and influencing engineering culture, standards, and best practices beyond a single team.
  • Side projects, open-source contributions, or other signals of curiosity and drive outside the scope of your day job.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$162,400—$290,000 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

raw.description:
Hello, we’re Instrumentl. 👋

Nonprofits do some of the most important work in the world, and most of them are still managing grants in spreadsheets. We're fixing that.

Instrumentl is a profitable, hypergrowth, YC-backed SaaS platform building the operating system for grant-funded organizations. More than 5,500 nonprofits use Instrumentl to discover, track, and win grant funding, from local community organizations to the San Diego Zoo and the University of Alaska. Collectively they’ve moved over $1 billion through our platform.

We're growing quickly, customers love us (check out our G2 reviews!), and we're hiring people who want to build something that matters.

About the role:

    You'll be our Senior Data Engineer, reporting to engineering leadership and taking ownership of a data platform that is still in its early stages. This is a high-ownership, build-from-the-foundation seat: you'll shape the architecture, stand up reliable pipelines and trusted data models, and set the engineering standards that let our data scale with the company. If you want real ownership over foundational infrastructure at a profitable, fast-growing company, rather than maintaining someone else's system at a larger one, this is that role.

What you'll do:

    Platform & Architecture

  • Design and scale our data platform across pipelines, models, and orchestration
  • Define and implement systems for data ingestion, storage, processing, and transformation
  • Optimize systems for performance, scalability, and cost from the start

    • Pipelines & Engineering Practices

  • Build scalable ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest from APIs, databases, and event streams
  • Apply software engineering principles such as testing, CI/CD, and modular design to data infrastructure
  • Establish best practices for data modeling, testing, and quality

    • Data Enablement & Partnership

  • Build the semantic layer and dashboards that make data usable across the company
  • Partner with engineering, product, and business teams to shape data requirements
  • Enable trusted, accessible data for BI and analytics decision-making

What you bring:

    Required

  • 5+ years building production software, with at least 2 to 3 of those focused on data engineering
  • Strong programming skills in Python and advanced proficiency in SQL
  • Proven experience building ETL/ELT pipelines end to end, from ingestion through serving
  • Hands-on experience with a cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and a modern data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, or Redshift)

    • Nice to have

  • Experience with workflow orchestration tools like Airflow
  • Experience supporting BI tools such as Looker or Tableau, and building semantic layers and dashboards
  • Deep fluency across the full data lifecycle: ingestion, storage, processing, transformation, and serving
  • Experience in early-stage or 0-to-1 environments

LeafLink is the largest unified B2B cannabis platform, providing licensed cannabis businesses a suite of tools to manage their business more effectively, sell or order from their favorite brands and accelerate growth. LeafLink processes more than $5 billion in wholesale cannabis orders annually.

Our team, backed by funding from leading VC's, including Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Nosara Capital, and Lerer Hippeau is poised to define the cannabis supply chain through technology. LeafLink was named one of Inc. 5000’s ‘Top 5000 Fastest-Growing Private Companies’; one of Fast Company's 'Top 10 Most Innovative Companies in Enterprise for 2020', joining the ranks of Amazon, Slack, and VMWare; one of Built In NYC's 'Best Places to Work in 2021'; 2024 Fast Company’s Best WorkPlaces for Innovators for Banking, Finance, and Fintech category; 2024 Green Market Report Award for Best Fintech in cannabis - and we're just getting started!

The Role

LeafLink is seeking a Business Operations Associate to work across an array of projects and cross-functional initiatives. Reporting directly to the Head of Business Operations, this role is highly versatile: you'll parachute into different parts of the business, clean up messy flows and processes, and plug into systems to get them running smoothly. You are as comfortable diving into data to find answers as you are rolling up your sleeves to execute directly.

You'll leverage both quantitative and qualitative data to shape strategy, drive decisions, and build buy-in across the organization. No task is too small: you don't mind digging into disparate, messy, or incomplete data, and you frequently raise your hand to pick up projects in need of an owner. This individual will spend meaningful time on our core marketplace and banking offerings, so experience or exposure to those verticals is a plus.

The position is fully remote.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Perform ad hoc market analyses and fill operational gaps
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of various SOPs and metrics for operations workflows, market launches, revenue-generating initiatives, and more
  • Lean-in to lead cross-functional initiatives across Sales, Marketing, Product, Operations, Public Policy, and Finance as needed
  • Communicate plans and outcomes to a broad range of internal stakeholders, both through written communications or presentations
  • Assist in identifying trends, patterns, and opportunities to enhance business performance and decision-making processes
  • Prepare biweekly reports on operational performance for key business lines, including marketplace and banking
  • Deep dive into data to identify trends, patterns, and opportunities, and translate findings into actionable recommendations
  • Clean up and improve existing operational processes and systems (e.g., CRM/data hygiene, reporting infrastructure) as gaps are identified

What You’ll Bring to the Team

  • 4-5 years of experience working at startups, preferably in FinTech or B2B platforms
  • High proficiency in Excel Salesforce, and Claude.ai, with the ability to analyze data and generate insights
  • Thrives in ambiguity and loves creating structure amid chaos
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented, with strong written and verbal communication skills
  • A bias toward action: you love problem-solving and are always looking for better, more efficient ways of doing things
  • Proven ability to coordinate and collaborate across multiple teams and stakeholders
  • A positive attitude and belief that no task is too small
  • You excel in a fast-paced startup, and you thrive in a market that is constantly evolving and changing
  • Knowledge or interest in the cannabis industry and related policy is a plus

  • A robust stock option plan to give our employees a direct stake in LeafLink’s success

  • Competitive compensation and 401k
  • Comprehensive healthcoverage (medical, dental, vision)
  • Commuter Benefits through our Flexible Spending Account

Senior Product Manager - Servicing (US Remote)

Why this Role Matters:

The Senior Product Manager - Servicing will own the product experience across Greenbox Capital’s servicing ecosystem, including both the tools used by internal team members and the experiences used by our customers.

This role is responsible for understanding business problems, customer needs, operational workflows, and team-member pain points, then translating those insights into scalable product solutions that improve efficiency, usability, and business outcomes.

You will serve as the architect of business impact, defining the problems we should solve, shaping the future-state experience, establishing requirements and success measures, and partnering closely with Technology to bring those solutions to life.

Salesforce is currently a key internal platform supporting servicing and may expand into additional areas of the business over time. While Salesforce experience is valuable, this is not a Salesforce administrator or technical architecture role. We are looking for a strong product leader who knows how to solve business problems from both the customer and team-member perspective.

In addition to owning the servicing experience, this role will support other strategic initiatives across the company through Greenbox Capital’s product pod structure.

This role reports to the Chief Operating Officer and works closely with Technology, Operations, Underwriting, Risk, Sales, Data, and other business teams.

What Success Looks Like:

Here’s how your time might break down (actual time can shift depending on business needs):

  • Servicing Product & Experience Ownership - Owning the roadmap and experience across customer-facing servicing capabilities and internal team-member tools
  • Product Discovery & Delivery - Identifying the right problems to solve and moving initiatives from discovery through development, launch, and iteration
  • Business Process & Workflow Optimization - Redesigning workflows, reducing friction, and identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, or improve how work gets done
  • Cross-Functional Product Leadership - Partnering across Product, Technology, Operations, Underwriting, Risk, Sales, and Data to solve high-priority business problems
  • Product Adoption & Business Impact - Ensuring new capabilities are adopted, used effectively, and produce measurable improvements in customer and business outcomes

How you’ll be measured:

Servicing Product & Experience Ownership:

  • Own and evolve the product roadmap for Greenbox Capital’s servicing experience
  • Develop a deep understanding of customer journeys, team-member workflows, operational challenges, and business needs
  • Define product priorities based on customer value, operational impact, business outcomes, effort, and strategic importance
  • Design future-state experiences and workflows that simplify processes and improve outcomes
  • Ensure internal tools and customer-facing experiences work cohesively across the servicing lifecycle

Product Discovery & Delivery:

  • Lead product initiatives from problem identification and discovery through launch and iteration
  • Conduct discovery with customers, team members, and business stakeholders to understand root problems before defining solutions
  • Translate complex business needs into clear product requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and measures of success
  • Maintain backlog clarity and establish thoughtful prioritization across competing initiatives
  • Partner closely with Technology throughout development, QA, release readiness, and implementation
  • Evaluate product performance after launch and drive continuous improvement based on data and user feedback

Business Process & Workflow Optimization:

  • Identify friction, unnecessary complexity, manual work, and breakdowns within servicing and operational workflows

raw.title: Senior Data Center Consultant
raw.excerpt: Summary of Job Role and ResponsibilitiesThe ideal Senior team member will provide leadership in many areas but specific to this position is the ability to support the analysis of data center infrastructure as part of our strategy development projects.
raw.description:
Summary of Job Role and Responsibilities

The ideal Senior team member will provide leadership in many areas but specific to this position is the ability to support the analysis of data center infrastructure as part of our strategy development projects. The skill sets are broken into 4 categories, Electrical, Mechanical, Operations, and Master Planning. The successful candidate must have these skills for the accurate completion of various data center “due diligence” tasks as part of an overall team conducting a data center strategy analysis for our client.

Electrical

  • Demonstrated expertise in interpreting electrical one-line diagrams and evaluating mission-critical electrical distribution systems, including utility service, switchgear, UPS, generators, transfer switches, PDUs, transformers, and grounding systems.
  • Strong understanding of electrical redundancy concepts (N, N+1, 2N, etc.), reliability principles, load calculations, power capacity, and identifying single points of failure with practical risk mitigation strategies.
  • Ability to assess the condition, operation, and maintenance effectiveness of critical power infrastructure, including UPS systems, battery systems, standby power, electrical distribution equipment, and associated controls.
  • Experience collecting, analyzing, and interpreting operational data from electrical infrastructure to evaluate system performance, reliability, energy efficiency, and compliance with industry best practices.
  • Working knowledge of the National Electrical Code (NEC), mission-critical facility design standards, and the ability to safely perform work in energized or critical infrastructure environments.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and computer skills, with the ability to serve as a trusted subject matter expert while preparing technical reports and using Microsoft Office applications.

Mechanical

  • Interpret mechanical one-line drawings and evaluate HVAC infrastructure in mission-critical facilities, from central cooling plants through CRAC/CRAH systems, while understanding redundancy concepts and calculating system load capacity.
  • Assess the condition, operation, and maintenance of mechanical infrastructure including chillers, cooling towers, heat rejection systems, pumps, valves, piping, thermal storage, and associated controls and instrumentation.
  • Analyze mechanical system designs to identify components, single points of failure, reliability risks, and energy optimization opportunities, providing practical recommendations to improve resilience, maintainability, and efficiency.
  • Collect, interpret, and analyze operational data from mechanical equipment and perform engineering calculations related to cooling capacity, power, kVA, power factor, and energy performance.
  • Apply industry best practices for mission-critical mechanical systems, including redundancy classifications, reliability principles (MTBF, MTTR, availability, maintainability), and safe work practices while effectively using Microsoft Office applications.
  • Serve as a confident, customer-facing mechanical subject matter expert, communicating technical findings and recommendations clearly while following written and verbal instructions.

Operations

  • Develop maintenance staffing plans and define the technical skill requirements needed to support mission-critical facility operations.
  • Operate and evaluate Building Monitoring and Control Systems (BMS/BAS) supporting critical mechanical and electrical infrastructure.
  • Assess the condition, maintenance practices, and documentation of mission-critical infrastructure, including raised floor environments, fire detection and suppression systems, and critical equipment records.
  • Evaluate operational processes including maintenance management, change management, and security systems to ensure reliability, compliance, and best practices.
  • Identify single points of failure, assess infrastructure reliability risks, and develop practical, cost-effective mitigation recommendations to improve data center availability.
  • Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge of mission-critical systems including Emergency Power Off (EPO), VESDA, FM-200, Ansul, sprinkler and pre-action systems, as well as physical security technologies such as card access, video surveillance, biometric access, and perimeter protection.

Conceptual Master Planning

  • Be able to evaluate the overall facility and provide input to such in the planning sessions and workshops
  • Working with Engineering/Design colleagues, assist in the development of conceptual designs for infrastructure expansion and/or capacity changes.
  • Possess a complete understanding redundancy requirements and Tier levels
  • Ability to evaluate the overall critical loading requirements for data center “greenfield” options
  • Ability to provide ROM (Rough Order of Magnitude) estimates (+/- 30%) for recommendations
  • Ability to present findings and interact with customers at all levels.

Other Skills and Knowledge

The Senior Data Center Consultant will demonstrate the following required abilities: • Managing and participating in the delivery of major projects – the candidate is expected to act as the client partner and project executive for all projects they develop. This will position the candidate to manage the project, its quality, and the client as a portfolio over time. The candidate will participate in delivery and will need to learn the use of the group’s analytic tools and support that need as required. The candidate will also manage the project to the forecast financial measures.

Presentation and Writing Skills: The candidate will need to communicate professionally, effectively, and persuasively in verbal and written form to client CIO/CFO/COO’s and other senior positions. In addition to client focused work, the candidate is expected to participate as an industry expert in symposiums, professional journals, and webinars.

Team-members generally work from their home office and travel when required. Travel can average 25%-50%, but there might be times when sustained travel over short periods of time are required, particularly when supporting our global projects.

It is desirable that the successful candidate have one or more of the following advanced requirements:

  • Applicable data center professional certifications
  • 10 Years + data center operational experience in privately owned or colocation facilities
  • BA/BS from an accredited College/University. Engineering or Computer Science degree is a plus.
  • Ability to pass a background check prior to offer letter
  • Hold a U.S. passport and travel internationally

Work at the heart of sustainable change

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. We believe sustainable change should create a thriving world for both nature and people. Our culture is grounded in openness, curiosity, responsibility, and respect for diverse perspectives.

Ready to join us?

If you are ready to bring your project leadership, technical judgment, and client management skills to a business focused on sustainable energy solutions, we invite you to apply.

Please submit your application and include your CV and any other relevant documents.

Ramboll in the Americas

Founded in Denmark, Ramboll is a foundation-owned people company. Ramboll has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices in the Americas, delivering innovative solutions within Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design. We invite you to contribute to a sustainable future working in an open, collaborative, and empowering company. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we together shape the societies of tomorrow.

Salary Transparency

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $125,000 to $155,000 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do. Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We are committed to equal employment opportunity, regardless of age, disability or medical condition, gender identity, marriage and domestic partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, ancestry, or national origin, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation, military service and veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at with such requests.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Position: Senior Data Center Consultant

EYP Mission Critical Facilities, part of Ramboll Americas Engineering, is an innovator and a market leader in sustainable Data Center Consulting & Strategy, Design, and Commissioning with a 25-year history of excellence in the industry. Numerous Fortune 500 companies, top tier universities, and global data center providers/investors, rely on EYP MCF to provide responsive solutions to today’s complex data center challenges. The Consulting groups core focus is to provide data center strategy analysis with the expertise to address the clients forward mission goals inclusive of their IT and Network architecture. The end goal is to develop a data center sourcing solution for our clients to use their existing facilities, colocation services, cloud services, or build new facilities. This includes developing a new data center topology, reliability and redundancy needs, and associated financial analysis for decision support requirements. The group also supports a wide range of data center assessment projects for investors looking to acquire data centers or develop them. Our growing team depends on motivated professionals with a flexible skill set and the ability to provide often unique, critical thinking to address the ever-changing landscape of data center design and operations.

raw.description:
Every great show has a stage manager: the person backstage calling every cue so the audience experiences only the performance. Product Operations plays that role for Mercury's product organization—building the operating systems, programs, and rhythms that let product teams spend less time navigating process and more time building radically different banking*.

We're looking for a Senior Product Operations Specialist to help scale the way Mercury builds products. You'll own some of our highest-impact operating programs—from launches and onboarding to product culture and organizational planning—while continually improving how they work as the company grows.

You'll partner closely with the Product Operations Manager and Product leadership to translate strategic direction into durable operating systems. Sometimes that means designing a new program from scratch. Other times it means taking something that's already working and making it dramatically better. You'll combine program leadership, operational judgment, and strong cross-functional relationships to ensure our product organization operates with clarity, consistency, and speed.

This is a role for someone who loves building leverage. Someone who sees operations not as administration, but as product design applied to how teams work.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own Mercury's Product Launch Program: Own Mercury's launch operating model, ensuring launches move through review with clear ownership, strong cross-functional coordination, and high quality. Continuously improve launch workflows, review processes, and retrospectives as Mercury scales.
  • Lead the New Grad PM Rotational Program: Own Mercury's rotational program for early-career Product Managers. Coordinate rotations, partner with managers and leadership, and evolve the program to deliver an exceptional development experience.
  • Build and Own PM Onboarding: Own the onboarding experience for new Product Managers, helping new hires ramp quickly through thoughtful programming, documentation, and peer connections. Continuously improve the experience based on feedback and organizational needs.
  • Drive Product Culture programming: Design and operate programs that strengthen Mercury's product culture, from internal rituals to external events and thought leadership. Partner across Product, Design, Communications, Recruiting, and People to create experiences that scale with the organization.
  • Drive Cross-Functional Programs: Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives across Product, Engineering, Design, Communications, Recruiting, and People. Create clarity, build alignment, and keep programs moving with momentum.

The ideal candidate for the role has:

  • 3–5 years of experience in Product Operations, Program Management, Business Operations, Chief of Staff, Consulting, or a similar cross-functional role, ideally supporting product or engineering organizations in a high-growth technology company.
  • A track record of owning cross-functional programs from concept through execution, balancing strategic thinking with exceptional operational follow-through.
  • Strong systems thinking. You naturally look beyond individual projects to design repeatable operating mechanisms that help organizations scale.
  • An instinct to improve rather than maintain. You don't simply inherit programs—you evolve them. You notice friction others have accepted and proactively make things simpler, faster, and more effective.
  • Excellent judgment and comfort operating in ambiguity. You can take a high-level objective and translate it into a clear plan, making thoughtful decisions where direction doesn't yet exist.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple concurrent initiatives while maintaining a consistently high bar for quality.
  • A product mindset. You approach internal operations the same way great product teams approach customer products—understanding user needs, measuring outcomes, iterating quickly, and continuously improving the experience.
  • A bias toward action paired with sound judgment. You know when speed matters, when quality matters, and how to balance both in a fast-moving environment.

The total rewards package at Mercury includes base salary, equity (stock options/RSUs), and benefits.

Our salary and equity ranges are highly competitive within the SaaS and fintech industry and are updated regularly using the most reliable compensation survey data for our industry. New hire offers are made based on a candidate’s experience, expertise, geographic location, and internal pay equity relative to peers.

  • US employees outside of the New York City, Los Angeles, Seattle, or the San Francisco Bay Area: $109,500 - $136,900

We are seeking a strategic, operationally-focused Director, Strategic Finance (Medicare Advantage) to serve as the primary financial architect for our core insurance business. This is a newly created, high-impact role designed for a leader who excels at the intersection of financial analysis, operational efficiency, and long-term value creation.

While you will sit within our centralized Finance organization, you will be deeply embedded in the Medicare Advantage (MA) leadership team. We are looking for a "high-agency" leader who can move beyond simple reporting to actively influence growth levers and unit economics.

As a Director, Strategic Finance (Medicare Advantage), you will:

  • Define, Measure, and Optimize Unit Economics: Partner with Actuarial, Growth, and Ops teams to develop a nuanced understanding of unit economics. You will define and track multi-year cohort and plan-level views, while most importantly, working to optimize unit costs and growth levers.
  • Lead Planning and Forecasting: Partner with leadership, actuarial and operations to develop annual plans and quarterly forecasts.
  • Drive the Business “Rhythm”: Partner with leadership to review core reporting and initiative progress consistently. You will leverage the monthly close process to ensure alignment with the budget and maintain rigorous scrutiny of ROI for all operational activities. Most importantly, you will ensure insights lead to action.
  • Evaluate Strategic Projects: Assess the value of high-stakes programs. Once capital is allocated, you will track these initiatives to ensure they deliver the projected value.

Success in this role looks like:

  • In the first 90 days: You have established financial clarity by owning the MA financial model and reporting cadence, providing leadership with a trusted view of performance, cost drivers, and unit economics.
  • In the first 6 months: You have raised the bar on discipline- cost center owners are actively managing spend against plan, and you have become the go-to partner for sophisticated initiative modeling and ROI tracking.
  • In the future: You have built a durable, scalable financial operating model where insights consistently inform investment decisions, enabling the MA business to grow efficiently and achieve sustainable national scale.

You should get in touch if:

  • Financial Expertise: You have 10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, specifically within healthcare, payer, or insurance environments.
  • Industry Knowledge: You possess deep experience with Medicare Advantage.
  • Strategic Thinking: You can connect complex actuarial data to operational outcomes and have a background in optimizing unit economics and capital allocation.
  • Executive Presence: You have a proven track record as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, able to influence strategy through data-driven storytelling and rigorous financial discipline.
  • Intellectual Agility: You thrive in evolving business models and have the ability to build scalable planning and governance frameworks from scratch.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Build the function. Shape the strategy. Help define the next chapter.

Since 2007, Clubspeed has been the leading venue management platform for the places people go to have fun. More than 1,700 venues across 34 countries rely on Clubspeed and Resova to power bookings, point of sale, integrated payments, memberships, waivers, guest experiences, and operations.

We're entering an exciting new chapter.

Following a recent acquisition, we're investing heavily across our products, leadership team, and go-to-market organization. As we scale, we're looking for our first Product Marketing Manager to build Product Marketing from the ground up.

This isn't a role where you'll inherit mature playbooks, positioning, or launch processes.

You'll create them.

If you love turning complex products into compelling stories, influencing product strategy, enabling sales, and building a world-class Product Marketing/Marketing function from scratch, we'd love to meet you.

The Opportunity

This is a foundational role that sits at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Leadership.

You'll define how we position our products, launch new capabilities, enable our commercial teams, and communicate the value we deliver to entertainment operators around the world.

You'll have significant ownership, executive visibility, and the opportunity to shape how Product Marketing evolves as we continue investing in growth.

If you're looking for a role where your work directly influences revenue, product strategy, and customer adoption, this is it.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, you'll:

  • Build the Product Marketing function and establish repeatable processes for launches, messaging, competitive intelligence, and sales enablement.
  • Create clear positioning and differentiated messaging across Clubspeed, Resova, and our integrated payments offering.
  • Become the voice of the customer by deeply understanding operators, buyers, and market trends.
  • Partner with Product to successfully launch new capabilities with measurable commercial impact.
  • Equip Sales and Customer Success with messaging, collateral, competitive insights, and training that improves win rates.
  • Build a repeatable product launch framework that scales with the business.
  • Help establish Product Marketing as a strategic partner across the organization.

What You'll Do

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and execute the go-to-market strategy for two key products, including positioning, messaging, competitive analysis, and audience targeting.
  • Own and manage marketing execution, including AI agent creation and management, content creation, campaign development, and lifecycle programs to drive customer engagement and growth.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with internal central marketing teams (e.g., Product, Sales, Demand Gen, Brand, Comms) to support execution of Behavioral Health marketing initiatives.
  • Build and manage Agents to deliver outsized returns and amplify your impact
  • Conduct market, customer, and competitive research to inform messaging and strategy.
  • Create marketing assets such as product one-pagers, sales enablement tools, website copy, case studies, email campaigns, and more.
  • Track and report on performance metrics, optimizing based on data and insights.
  • Establish foundational processes and frameworks for product marketing to scale efforts over time.
  • Serve as the voice of the product internally and externally, ensuring a consistent narrative across all touchpoints.
  • Create and manage marketing budget; allocating resources effectively across various marketing channels to achieve goals, maximizing ROI.
  • Manage tradeshow/event planning and execution for industry events and conferences

Requirements

What We're Looking For

You'll likely be successful if you have:

  • 5–7 years of experience in product marketing, content creation, or a related marketing function, preferably in B2B, tech, or scale up environments.
  • You have created and launched your own AI projects to let you focus on the stuff AI isn’t great at yet
  • Proven success developing and executing GTM strategies and campaigns from scratch.
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to juggle strategy and execution.
  • Experience working cross-functionally and managing agency, freelancer, and vendor relationships.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a sharp eye for compelling storytelling.
  • A collaborative, proactive, and flexible mindset.
  • Self-starter comfortable operating in ambiguity and building processes from the ground up.

Experience with payments, commerce platforms, point of sale, reservations, hospitality, or vertical SaaS is a significant advantage.

You'll Thrive Here If...

  • You enjoy building more than maintaining.
  • You're energized by blank sheets of paper and undefined problems.
  • You naturally connect Product, Marketing, and Sales.
  • You care as much about business outcomes as marketing metrics.
  • You ask "why" before deciding "how."
  • You like moving quickly, experimenting, and improving.
  • You enjoy working directly with senior leaders and influencing company strategy.
  • You want your work to directly impact revenue growth.

Benefits

  • Competitive base salary (between $85,000-$95,000 CAD)
  • Comprehensive health coverage, including dental and vision
  • Flexible time off policy
